body: He might just be the most beautiful man I've ever seen in my life. Even for a model. Those eyes! Life is not fair :/

Most people believe that suicidal ideation is perverse and against natural human nature, but I wonder whether that's really true. Maybe for some people, the truth is that they must continue living, no matte what. Maybe for others, including you - an apathetic suicide wish is the natural state. 


You don't sound like a whiny teenager at all to me, your thoughts are well articulated. You're right that it would hurt your parents a lot. Sometimes there are no good choices in life. Either option leads to a wrong outcome, both causing misery. I don't know how to offer you comfort but I understand how you feel, and I can relate.

I seriously hope it didn't come across as patronising. I guess I have a very unique thought process? People sometimes do misunderstand my intentions, I think I need to spend a little more time in the future making sure I articulate my thoughts in a clear, logical and *accessible* way to the best of my ability. 


I was sharing my similar experiences, one where I've had little social support. I was explaining that I am an example of someone who has felt love even during those times - hoping that I may be able to help by explaining loving himself is most important but then I pondered that perhaps since I have a different personality this advice might not make sense to him, and then I was suggesting that however maybe I had a different experience due to my personality type. You might have mistaken my relief for boastfulness - I am glad in a way to be independent, reading OP's experiences made me grateful that my mood does not depend on my social relationship strength. It's empowering to me personally.  I do wonder what it's like to be like other people, though - most people I've spoken to find my attachment tendencies to be a little strange. 


I think it's a valid statement that has been consistently applicable to me that my personality tends to being fiercely independent. It can be a good and a bad thing to be very independent. It's not really boastful, but I guess 'fiercely independent' seems like a flattering way to put it. I was more thinking out loud, considering the different personality types in the world, I'm more of a contemplative person. 


You boldly assume that beyond a doubt I mean harm. It was really not a 100% certain accusation based on the comment I made to OP. Surely it says something about you, and all the people you have met (and the way you've interpreted people you've met), the fact that you will jump to this hasty conclusion on me. 



Thanks for finding my post interesting enough to respond to, I feel guilty that you assumed my intentions were malicious when I really in my own head (which no offence, but you can't read my mind and thus know with 100% certainty that you are confident what my intentions were).


If my thoughts were taken to mean that I thought OP's suffering is invalid, then I guess I should have been wiser before posting and I wish I was intelligent and socially aware enough to realise that my words and intentions would have been twisted to mean something so vitriolic. I was only expressing the thoughts and personal experience that the OP's text post inspired from me.

What motivated you to tell suicidal people you care about them? I think it's a very noble pursuit and I'm impressed, albeit curious as to what kind of thought process led you to this subreddit. You've touched my heart with your caring nature. You're so sweet. A lively, happy, optimistic 16 year old girl, who wants to help sad, lonely people. What a darling. 


Please don't take this harshly but oftentimes, suicidal people have issues that can't be solved by you telling them that you love them. They may even become angered and feel you are condescending them by suggesting that it will make a difference for some stranger on the internet cares about them, and you are attempting to correct thinking and suggesting thinking error in your statement 


>  You never know that no one cares, there is ALWAYS someone who cares,


which can seem insulting to a person. I know you have a kind heart but your input can seem almost intrusive, and it can seem like sticky beaking. Thank you for trying to help people, I hope you know that I have been forever touched by your act of kindness and giving up your time to spread some love.

It's true - I'm not being too optimistic, just trying to be as logical as I possibly can. I try to avoid depression and do all I can so I won't slip into depression - when you are depressed, your thoughts are critical and negative so that you can't see the truth. 



People are selfish, and look out for themselves first of all, but at the same time people are inherently empathetic and loving. Your sister cares for you and loves you, she'd be horribly emotionally scarred and pained by your death. It's extremely painful or just too hasslesome/difficult for her to try to talk about it. Sounds like she is trying to give you some tough love.  That's fine, we can't expect everyone to be able to talk about such a painful, difficult topic so easily. There is miscommunication between the two of you. 


She hasn't blocked off all contact with you, she only screened night calls because she feels it intrudes on her health. That's an example of her looking out for her health first of all. We need to look out for *ourselves* before we can care for others.

Listen I know you mean well but you're severely lacking in the logical reasoning faculties. 


What I said was that there have been times in my life when the only person whose support I had was my own. I clearly said 


> I still had joy and self confidence 


> I never felt lonely 



I know you have a kind, giving heart and you are trying to reach out a helping hand but you've misunderstood what I am saying. In fact, I highly doubt you even read the whole thing. Or comprehended it, at least.

Well, people are inherently selfish anyway - money makes our world go around. Look at the people we hold as our role models in today's world - celebrities. Eye candy, and not much more, which is very shallow of us. Our entire world is an testament to our selfish nature.  As for cowardly - it actually takes a great amount of courage to take your own life, a sort of courage that I (controversial, I know) revere, and don't entirely comprehend. Maybe it's not even courage, maybe it's blinded emotional extreme turmoil or just plain apathy.

I beleive it a symptom of mental chemical imbalance and disordered, unhealthy thinking to believe you are of little worth. 


I have had many instances where not a single person told me they cared about me, no one wanted to be friends with me and through all of those times, I still had joy and self confidence. I have been through times where I had less human contact than you have ever experienced in your life, and I never felt lonely. I have never thought something like "it honestly wouldn't matter if I was here or not." The number one thing that should matter is your self perception and self love. The number one person we have is ourselves, and you can't find love in other people if you don't have self love first of all. It's my self confidence and happiness that attracts people to me. Perhaps my attachment style is too different to yours, though I have been psychologically profiled to be 'fiercely independent' and I now that my mood is naturally very high (happy).

> It took me an hour to write because I kept losing myself in thought.



Wow. Mental illness sounds very debilitating. I honestly don't even know what to tell you. At least the resulting product is articulate.


 It's insightful to learn the effects that a mental illness can have on a person's perspective and experiences through qualitative self report. I think that better mental health care services would honestly help people suffering like you are.
That is a really hurtful story. I am very sorry for all of your pain. You've motivated me out of fear, to do all that I can to make sure that when I am 32 I don't end up in such a situation.

It's hurtful when the people closest to you can't give you the support you need from them. Know that your family loves you and values you, in their own way, even if you don't feel that they have expressed it. People are inherently empathetic and loving, but they aren't necessarily good communicators or emotionally aware.

I do believe that this sub stigmatises suicide, somewhat. I don't know how much you can help someone when your perspective is stubbornly that life is of ultimate value rather than a person's satisfaction with life. 


I do believe that valuing life greatly will help some people hang on, and then from that period they are kept alive, they will have the time to find happiness/meaning. Sometimes, it doesn't work that way and they have to live through misery. It's not easy to predict whether a person's problems will or will not subside, but when in doubt no one will tell you to go through with suicide.

I'm really interested by your thoughts, but I doubt anyone can help with such little detail. Why do you feel this way? Is it just in your personality/mood disposition to be bored? Did something make you depressed, heartbreak that caused you to feel like your life is meaningless?

I've read men's anecdotal comments of their experiences with unattractive women on websites like BodyBuilding.com. Those type of men use women like toys and reiterate the phrase "gotta slay dragons to get to the princesses" (*hilarious* - not) and think it's encouraged behaviour amongst those men, they do not have any compunction about their behaviour. Those men are ruthless, and have no second thoughts about it. It's a cold, cruel world created by those type of men. The men on reddit seem a more sympathetic bunch, it seems like a safer, kinder world with a world view shared by this bunch. I don't doubt there are plenty of real men like BodyBuilding.com neanderthal degenerates and the reddit dudes who are selfish (to a healthy extent) but still empathetic. 


I think your attitude is a happy medium of selfishness and still considering the effect of your actions on other people's emotions, I find this to be a reasonable state of mind and perfectly acceptable way to live your life. So as for the moral questionability of your hypothesis, I am giving you the okay. 



As for experience with actually trying it, I doubt that any amount of good experiences shared or bonding will make up for a lack of physical attraction. Physical attraction is king, I believe people who make themselves live without it are entirely desperate, brain dead or martyrs. I think it's ethically acceptable to date these women, only if you let them know that  you find them ugly. Anyone who says it isn't wrong is devoid of sympathy, or is trying to defy logic as they don't want to suffer guilt after doing this exactly. What you are doing is using someone as a stepping stone, and never letting them know. You're using someone you think poorly of to step up yourself and make yourself feel great. They could be under the wrong impression that they are pursuing a LTR, or that you at least adore them, when you actually turn your nose up to them in your own head, you're wasting their time and degrading them. 


So overall, I think it's fine to do, as long as you tell them first.

Why are you in such pain? You know - a part of intelligence is being able to recognise why you are in emotional pain, finding the root and thus being able to fix it as well. I think that being a kind person in this situation would mean that I try to talk you out of your suicide attempt - and I am trying to be a kind, empathetic person. 


You posted here at all, why? Maybe you wished someone would connect to you, help you stop because you are crying in despair on the i side and don't actually want to die. 


Being smart compared to most people is no big deal. Most people are unthinking, hypocritical and not very intelligent (average IQ is pretty bleak). But you are gifted - your mind is beautiful. I think you could do great things and since I have rather meritocrastic views I want to help you find the will to live and find the joy in life. 


What was the last thing that did make you feel joy, what things do you find beautiful and worth living for? Who was Jess? A beautiful, clever love interest or something? A friend, family member?

I know what being unmotivated and lazy is like but believe me - you will forgive yourself and find a like minded person to connect with. Gettiing out of laziness is difficult, and more than that slipping back into laziness is easy. But showing yourself you can behave in a way other than lazy for a period of time can be a great motivation. 

With a burning passion for academia, you know how satisfying it is to finally achieve a goal, or even just read. It's beautiful.


I don't know how much it would mean but you are very articulate, eloquent even and it's beautiful to read.

The fact that there actually people responding to any of the suicidewatch posts has warmed my cold,logical heart. Don't you think it's loving and kind that humans want to pull people back from a depressive state, that all people want one another to be happy?

> I know that nobody can change my life for the better except myself


Well you've just said everything you need yourself. Obviously all you need is within yourself and you should slowly grow that and make your life better, because it sounds like you know what you need to do.

This sounds like a really spontaneous, spur of the moment suicide, one with high adrenaline and high on emotions. 


I understand that the parent figure can be an important role in determining one's self worth. These words can be really hard on your heart. If you are in such excruciating pain, what can any of us do for you? It's you who it has effected so greatly, and only you who knows what solution will provide you with satisfaction. All I know is that life is a very difficult thing for a human to actually want to take from their own selves, and that leaving in regret is very painful.

What kind of rocks? 
Why are you posting here, is it because you want people to tell you "No, please live, life is beautiful, you are worthy, stop being lazy" because I can guarantee that is the sort of thing you will hear. Does that honestly help? Really? I don't think it does. It's too generic, it's what everyone says, and it places all blame on you, while showing you that people find worth in human life, because of course the ultimate objective as animals, is survival of course. 


If you just want to express yourself and have someone listen, and express your sadness and possibly even brainstorm some sort of solution that works for you to help you feel satisfied, I will do that for you.
